rubrics.body:
Criterion `body` (body anatomy):
- 5: Every visible body part is anatomically correct in all frames: right number of arms, legs, hands and
  fingers; joints bend naturally; proportions are human.
- 4: Anatomy correct overall; one small, brief flaw (e.g. fingers merged in one or two frames, a hand
  slightly blurred) that is only seen on close inspection.
- 3: A clear anatomical error in some frames: a malformed or extra/missing hand, a limb bending the wrong
  way, a limb briefly merging with the body or an object.
- 2: Clear anatomical errors in most frames, or several different errors.
- 1: The body is broken throughout: melted, fused or missing limbs, extra limbs, or a non-human shape.
rubrics.face:
Criterion `face` (face quality):
- 5: The face is sharp, undistorted and stable in all frames where it is visible; eyes, nose and mouth
  are well-formed.
- 4: The face is good; slight softness or a tiny flaw in one or two frames.
- 3: Clear distortion in some frames: asymmetric or smeared features, flickering eyes or mouth, the face
  changing shape.
- 2: The face is distorted or smeared in most frames.
- 1: No recognizable face where one should be, or the face is badly deformed throughout.
- (If the face is not visible in any frame — person seen from behind or too small — give 3 and say so.)
rubrics.temporal:
Criterion `temporal` (temporal consistency):
- 5: Person, clothing and scene stay consistent across all frames; nothing appears, disappears, changes
  colour or melts.
- 4: One minor inconsistency (e.g. a small object or a texture detail changes slightly).
- 3: A clear inconsistency in some frames: clothing colour or pattern shifts, an object appears or
  vanishes, the background warps.
- 2: Several clear inconsistencies, or one that lasts most of the clip.
- 1: The content changes throughout: identity, clothing or scene morph from frame to frame.
rubrics.physics:
Criterion `physics` (physical plausibility of the person):
- 5: Movement is physically plausible: feet are planted when bearing weight, no floating, no sliding, no
  passing through objects or the ground; speed and balance look natural.
- 4: Plausible overall; one subtle issue (e.g. slight foot sliding in one step).
- 3: A clear issue in some frames: feet sliding or floating above the ground, a limb passing through an
  object, an impossible balance.
- 2: Clear issues in most frames.
- 1: Movement is physically impossible throughout (floating, teleporting, constant sliding).
rubrics.integration:
Criterion `integration` (person composited into the scene):
- 5: The person looks filmed in the scene: lighting direction and colour match the scene, correct
  shadows, correct scale and perspective, feet in contact with the ground, correct occlusion with scene
  objects.
- 4: Looks filmed in the scene, but one subtle cue is off on close inspection (e.g. a slightly soft or
  faint shadow, a small colour cast).
- 3: One clear compositing cue in some frames: missing shadow, lighting from a different direction,
  feet briefly floating, wrong occlusion.
- 2: Several cues, or one cue in most frames: the person looks like a cut-out placed on the scene.
- 1: Clearly composited throughout: wrong scale or perspective, floating, a visible edge or halo around
  the person.
rubrics.identity_face:
Criterion `identity_face` (same face as the reference identity):
- 5: The face clearly belongs to the same person as in the reference: face shape, skin tone, eyes, nose,
  mouth, facial hair and apparent age and gender all match.
- 4: Same person; one minor difference (e.g. slightly different face shape or skin tone).
- 3: Plausibly the same person but with a clear difference in one feature (different facial hair,
  noticeably different age or face shape).
- 2: Most facial features differ; resembles the reference only in broad traits (gender, skin tone).
- 1: A different person.
- (If the face is not visible in the output, give 3 and say so.)
rubrics.identity_outfit:
Criterion `identity_outfit` (same appearance as the reference identity (clothing, hair, accessories)):
- 5: Every clothing item, colour, pattern, logo, accessory and the hairstyle match the reference.
- 4: All main items match; one small detail differs or is missing (a small logo, a bracelet, a shade of
  colour).
- 3: One main item clearly differs (different colour of a garment, missing jacket, different hair
  length) while the rest match.
- 2: Several main items differ; only a few match.
- 1: The appearance is unrelated to the reference.
rubrics.scene_match:
Criterion `scene_match` (same scene as the given scene video (ignore the person)):
- 5: Same place: layout, objects, colours, lighting and camera motion all match the scene frames.
- 4: Same place; one minor difference (a small object changed, slight colour or lighting shift).
- 3: Recognizably the same place but with a clear difference: an object added or removed, a different
  camera motion, a noticeably different colour grading.
- 2: Only broadly similar (same type of place), with most details different.
- 1: A different place.
rubrics.action_match:
Criterion `action_match` (same action as the reference motion):
- 5: The person performs the same action as the reference throughout, with the same phases in the same
  order and timing (e.g. steps, turn, wave).
- 4: Same action and phases; small timing or amplitude differences.
- 3: The main action matches but one phase is missing, added or clearly mistimed.
- 2: Only partially related (e.g. walking vs running, or one of two actions missing).
- 1: A different action, or the person does not perform the action at all.
rubrics.pose_match:
Criterion `pose_match` (same body pose frame by frame):
- 5: In every compared frame the body pose matches the reference: torso orientation, arm and leg
  positions, including which side (left/right) is doing what.
- 4: Matches in nearly all frames; small differences in a limb's angle.
- 3: Clear mismatch in some frames (a limb in a clearly different position, the torso facing a different
  direction).
- 2: Mismatch in most frames, or left and right limbs swapped.
- 1: Poses are unrelated to the reference.
rubrics.trajectory_match:
Criterion `trajectory_match` (same movement through the image):
- 5: The person moves through the frame along the same path as the reference: same direction, same
  turns, same distance to the camera over time, same position in the frame.
- 4: Same path; small offsets in position or distance.
- 3: Same overall direction but a clear difference (a turn missing, moving toward instead of along the
  camera, a clearly different position in the frame).
- 2: Clearly different path, with only one aspect matching.
- 1: Unrelated path (e.g. standing still vs walking across, or opposite direction).
rubrics.text_match:
Criterion `text_match` (matches the caption):
- 5: Every element of the caption is shown: the person, their actions in the stated order, and any
  stated objects or setting.
- 4: All main elements shown; one minor detail missing or different.
- 3: The main action is shown, but a stated element is missing or wrong.
- 2: Only partly related to the caption.
- 1: Unrelated to the caption.
